outputText:
claim: >-
  A complete read-only inspection of the four retained VS Code files yields five
  bounded, transferable lessons, chiefly reinforcing Get Modular's accepted
  separation between a deterministic semantic compiler and a privileged
  product host. The evidence does not support adopting VS Code, importing its
  runtime architecture, changing Get Modular semantics, accepting any proposed
  ADR, or starting Core implementation. This result can close the new O1
  source-inspection follow-up, while historical O1 records remain
  source-unavailable.

authority:
  precedence:
    - >-
      Accepted Get Modular authority controls. ARCH-SYSTEM-BOUNDARY assigns
      declarations, bindings, deterministic graph compilation, bounded
      diagnostics, immutable plans, and digests to Core, while authorization,
      loading, readiness, generations, routing, drain, and recovery remain
      product-host responsibilities
      (gm/docs/architecture/system-boundary.md:13-15,33-45,60-74,85-93).
    - >-
      ADR-0001 forbids DI-container types, discovery, global registries, product
      types, plugin types, and executable imports in the production API
      (gm/docs/decisions/0001-product-neutral-deterministic-module-composition.md:28-48).
    - >-
      ADR-0004 fixes exact inert identities, complete profiles, explicit
      required/optional/ordered-many bindings, and dependency order as graph
      data rather than lifecycle commands
      (gm/docs/decisions/0004-freeze-v1-portable-composition-contract-and-plan-digest.md:28-75,77-111).
    - >-
      ADR-0005 through ADR-0007 control compatibility, bounded deterministic
      failures, normalization, resource limits, and executable qualification;
      static or reviewed evidence does not establish production conformance
      (ADR-0005:28-108; ADR-0006:76-120; ADR-0007:363-425).
    - >-
      ADR-0008 permits bounded build-time self-composition but deliberately
      leaves host, loader, resolver, and independent conformance machinery in a
      privileged kernel (ADR-0008:52-77,100-164,253-285).
    - >-
      ADR-0015 permits only governed private source after an explicit
      product-owner start record; it does not itself start implementation
      (ADR-0015:64-122). The readiness report says that record and enforcement
      are absent, so private Core remains NO-GO
      (gm/research/implementation-readiness/report.md:5-19,573-599).
  nonAuthority:
    - >-
      gm/docs/architecture/current-contract.md is active derived guidance and
      explicitly cannot replace accepted ADRs (lines 27-29).
    - >-
      The readiness report, fixtures, models, and this inspection are evidence,
      not acceptance authority or expert consensus
      (report.md:75-102,355-365,556-569).
    - >-
      The retained VS Code files are supplemental source inputs only, not
      executable evidence, adoption approval, or Get Modular authority
      (oss/source-manifest.json:2-5).

observedBehavior:
  evidenceClass: source-inspection-only
  executedEvidence: none
  identity: >-
    VS Code preserves an extension identifier's display spelling but derives a
    lowercase lookup key in ExtensionIdentifier.equals/toKey. An optional UUID
    appears in description types and comments, but the retained equality
    implementation does not prove UUID reconciliation.
  declarationsAndDependencies: >-
    The manifest co-locates inert contributions with executable entrypoints,
    activation events, extension dependencies, affinities, capabilities, and
    target metadata. Activation recursively creates dependency operations;
    unknown dependencies and failed activations prevent consumer activation.
    Dependencies without main/browser entrypoints are treated as descriptive
    and skipped during activation.
  activationOrderAndScopes: >-
    Dependency operations complete before the dependent activates, while
    independent requested extensions and host managers use Promise.all. Events
    are cached and replayed after initialization or restart. Placement is
    explicitly host-owned across local process, local web worker, and remote
    locations; immediate remote activation may be deferred until readiness.
  lifecycleUnloadAndUpgrades: >-
    Installation, update, uninstall, enablement, and profile changes feed a
    serialized mutable-registry delta queue. Updates can remove the prior
    identity before adding the replacement. Activated extensions cannot be
    dynamically removed through canRemoveExtension. Shutdown disconnects whole
    hosts in reverse creation order; remote crashes may restart a host and
    replay requested events.
  compatibilityIsolationAndErrors: >-
    Manifest metadata exposes engines.vscode, target platform, extension kind,
    virtual-workspace and untrusted-workspace support. Enabled/proposed-API and
    workspace-trust filtering occur in host services. Activation failures use
    ordinary Error objects, raw messages, causes and stacks; runtime errors are
    retained in mutable status. The subset does not show enforcement of engine
    ranges, executable loading, process isolation, or complete upgrade custody.

applicability:
  transferableLessons:
    - >-
      Identity: define one explicit equality/indexing rule and use it
      consistently. For Get Modular that rule remains accepted exact validated
      ASCII identity—not VS Code case folding, aliases, or UUID equivalence.
    - >-
      Declarations: preserve the separation between inert contribution metadata
      and executable entrypoints. Get Modular should continue emitting only an
      immutable semantic plan; a product adapter maps authorized factories or
      loaders afterward.
    - >-
      Dependencies: validate the complete dependency world and cycles before
      construction, and propagate dependency failure explicitly. Get Modular
      does this deterministically at compile time; it must not inherit VS Code's
      activation-operation machinery.
    - >-
      Scopes and order: distinguish dependency-before-consumer graph order from
      operational placement and activation. Local/worker/remote selection,
      readiness, replay, and concurrency belong to a product host.
    - >-
      Lifecycle and failures: require future hosts to specify update, unload,
      restart, cleanup, and failure propagation independently of Core. Mutable
      host state and runtime Error telemetry must remain separate from Get
      Modular's bounded deterministic diagnostics.
  nonTransferableRisks:
    - "Case-insensitive or UUID-aliased identity would contradict accepted exact GM coordinates."
    - "A mutable global registry or service/DI decorator would create a second authority."
    - "Activation events, implicit discovery, affinity, and registration timing are ambient host policy."
    - "Skipping descriptive dependencies cannot replace required/optional/ordered-many capability bindings."
    - "Registry versionId is not CandidateGenerationId, RuntimeGenerationId, fencing, or routing authority."
    - "Raw Error messages, stacks, clocks, retries, and telemetry are unsuitable for deterministic Core diagnostics."

benefits:
  - "Reinforces the already accepted compiler-versus-host boundary with concrete source examples."
  - "Supports inert metadata and executable-loader separation without adopting VS Code's manifest."
  - "Highlights dependency-failure, scope, unload, and restart cases future product-host tests must cover."
  - "Provides pinned O1 source inspection while preserving historical evidence custody."

failureModes:
  - "Treating activation order as plan semantics would make results depend on events, readiness, and concurrency."
  - "Copying the mutable delta registry would undermine immutable-plan and permutation guarantees."
  - "Copying hot-update behavior would leave activated implementations non-removable and provide no generation fencing."
  - "Copying runtime errors into Core would leak arbitrary extension messages or stacks and break bounded ordering."
  - "Inferring isolation from local/worker/remote labels would overclaim; the retained host implementation is incomplete."

counterexamples:
  - "A declared dependency with neither main nor browser is not activated (extHostExtensionActivator.ts:296-301)."
  - "Dependency loops are removed and extensions disabled by a registry result, not returned as a GM-style bounded SCC plan failure (abstractExtensionService.ts:320-329,573-579)."
  - "Reverse host shutdown follows creation/connection needs, not dependencyOrder (abstractExtensionService.ts:1353-1363)."
  - "An activated extension cannot be removed safely through the dynamic delta path (abstractExtensionService.ts:392-405)."
  - "Extension identifier lookup is case-insensitive, unlike Get Modular's exact accepted identity algebra."

confidence:
  sourceInspection: high
  transferableBoundaryLessons: high
  productWideClaims: low
  executedBehavior: none
  rationale: >-
    Every retained file was read completely and concrete functions were
    inspected, but the subset is narrow and none of it was built or executed.

recommendedDecision: >-
  Record this as a new bounded O1 read-only source-inspection result at the
  manifest-pinned VS Code commit. Close only the previously missing source-access
  follow-up lane; retain historical source-unavailable classifications unchanged.
  Carry the five lessons as corroborating design constraints, not new authority.
  Do not adopt VS Code, accept a decision, implement Core, or expand Get Modular
  into a host, lifecycle manager, container, compatibility resolver, or plugin
  runtime.

conditionsToReverse:
  - "The retained bytes or manifest provenance fail independent coordinator verification."
  - "A broader pinned source set or executed probe contradicts a stated observation."
  - "Accepted successor authority changes Get Modular's compiler/host boundary or identity algebra."
  - "A product-owned host requirement demonstrates that one rejected operational behavior belongs in a separately governed adapter."
  - "Future evidence proves a narrower transferable mechanism without importing mutable registry or lifecycle authority."
